name: Paradise Lost · Gustave Doré
description: Edición anotada en verso: las notas de Verity al pie de página y las cincuenta láminas de Doré · An annotated verse edition: Verity's notes at the foot of the page and Doré's fifty plates
credits: Milton · Verity · Doré · Project Gutenberg · Wikisource · Wikimedia Commons

resources.caption: Him the almighty Power / Hurled headlong flaming from the ethereal sky
resources.altText: The fall of the rebel angels, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Forthwith upright he rears from off the pool / His mighty stature
resources.altText: Satan rises from the burning lake, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: They heard, and were abashed, and up they sprung
resources.altText: Satan rouses his legions, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: So numberless were those bad Angels seen / Hovering on wing under the cope of Hell
resources.altText: The fallen angels on the wing, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Their summons called, / From every band and squared regiment, / By place or choice the worthiest
resources.altText: The council summoned to Pandemonium, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: High on a throne of royal state, which far / Outshone the wealth of Ormus and of Ind
resources.altText: Satan enthroned, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Gorgons, and Hydras, and Chimeras dire
resources.altText: The fallen angels explore Hell, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Before the gates there sat / On either side a formidable Shape
resources.altText: Satan meets Sin and Death, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: With head, hands, wings, or feet, pursues his way, / And swims, or sinks, or wades, or creeps, or flies
resources.altText: Satan’s journey through Chaos, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Heaven rung / With jubilee, and loud Hosannas filled / The eternal regions
resources.altText: The Son and the hosts of Heaven, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: And many more too long, / Embryos and idiots, eremites and friars
resources.altText: The Paradise of Fools, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Toward the coast of Earth beneath, / Down from the ecliptic, sped with hoped success, / Throws his steep flight in many an aery wheel
resources.altText: Satan flies down to the Earth, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Me miserable! which way shall I fly / Infinite wrath and infinite despair?
resources.altText: Satan’s despair, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Now to the ascent of that steep savage hill / Satan had journeyed on, pensive and slow
resources.altText: Satan above Eden, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: A happy rural seat of various view
resources.altText: Satan surveys the Garden, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: The savoury pulp they chew, and in the rind, / Still as they thirsted, scoop the brimming stream
resources.altText: Adam and Eve in the Garden, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: So promised he; and Uriel to his charge / Returned
resources.altText: Gabriel at the gate of Eden, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: These to the bower direct / In search of whom they sought
resources.altText: Ithuriel and Zephon, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Nor more; but fled / Murmuring, and with him fled the shades of night
resources.altText: Satan flees Gabriel, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Leaning half-raised, with looks of cordial love / Hung over her enamoured
resources.altText: Adam wakes Eve, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Eastward among those trees, what glorious shape / Comes this way moving
resources.altText: Raphael comes to the Garden, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: To whom the winged Hierarch replied: / O Adam, one Almighty is, from whom / All things proceed
resources.altText: Raphael instructs Adam and Eve, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: This greeting on thy impious crest receive
resources.altText: Abdiel strikes Satan, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Now storming fury rose, / And clamour such as heard in Heaven till now / Was never
resources.altText: The war in Heaven, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Then Satan first knew pain, / And writhed him to and fro
resources.altText: Satan wounded, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Now Night her course began
resources.altText: Night on the field of battle, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: On the foughten field / Michaël and his Angels, prevalent / Encamping, placed in guard their watches round
resources.altText: Michael’s angels keep watch, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Nine days they fell
resources.altText: The rebel angels cast out, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Hell at last, / Yawning, received them whole
resources.altText: The fall into Hell, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Wave rolling after wave, where way they found, / If steep, with torrent rapture
resources.altText: The waters gathered, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: And God said, Let the waters generate / Reptile with spawn abundant, living soul; / And let fowl fly above the earth
resources.altText: The creation of the fish and the fowl, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: And seems a moving land, and at his gills / Draws in, and at his trunk spouts out, a sea
resources.altText: Leviathan, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Meanwhile the tepid caves, and fens, and shores, / Their brood as numerous hatch
resources.altText: The birds hatched, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: And now on Earth the seventh / Evening arose in Eden
resources.altText: The evening of the seventh day, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: So parted they, the Angel up to Heaven / From the thick shade, and Adam to his bower
resources.altText: Raphael takes his leave, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: In with the river sunk, and with it rose / Satan
resources.altText: Satan returns with the river, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: O Earth, how like to Heaven, if not preferred / More justly
resources.altText: Satan’s soliloquy, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Him fast sleeping soon he found, / In labyrinth of many a round self-rolled
resources.altText: Satan finds the serpent, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Nearer he drew, and many a walk traversed / Of stateliest covert, cedar, pine, or palm
resources.altText: The serpent draws near Eve, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Back to the thicket slunk / The guilty Serpent
resources.altText: Eve eats the fruit, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Nor only tears / Rained at their eyes, but high winds worse within / Began to rise
resources.altText: Adam and Eve after the Fall, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: They heard, / And from his presence hid themselves among / The thickest trees
resources.altText: Adam and Eve hide, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: And now expecting / Each hour their great Adventurer from the search / Of foreign worlds
resources.altText: The fallen angels await Satan, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Dreadful was the din / Of hissing through the hall, thick-swarming now / With complicated monsters
resources.altText: The fallen angels turned to serpents, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: This said, they both betook them several ways
resources.altText: Sin and Death set out, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: The heavenly bands / Down from a sky of jasper lighted now / In Paradise
resources.altText: Michael’s band descends, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Began to build a vessel of huge bulk
resources.altText: The building of the Ark, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: All dwellings else / Flood overwhelmed, and them with all their pomp / Deep under water rolled
resources.altText: The Flood, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: They beseech / That Moses might report to them his will, / And terror cease
resources.altText: Moses with the tables of the Law, by Gustave Doré

resources.caption: Some natural tears they dropped, but wiped them soon
resources.altText: The expulsion from Eden, by Gustave Doré
The fall of the rebel angels, by Gustave Doré
The expulsion from Eden, by Gustave Doré
